title: Equitable Mortgage & Property Redemption Rights in Bangladesh (1882 Act)

heroIntro: When borrowing against urban flats or ancestral land in Bangladesh, banks routinely create either an Equitable Mortgage by deposit of title deeds (Section 58(f)) or a Registered Mortgage with Irrevocable Power of Attorney (Section 59). Under Section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882, every mortgagor holds an inviolable statutory Right of Redemption upon clearing principal and lawful interest—meaning a lender cannot permanently forfeit your land or withhold original title deeds after repayment.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Property Mortgage & Redemption in Bangladesh
quickAnswer.text: Section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 guarantees return of original deeds and cancellation of mortgage upon full payment.
points: Governing Laws: Transfer of Property Act 1882 (Sections 58–104), Registration Act 1908 (Section 17) & Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003
Registered vs. Equitable Mortgage: Deposit of title deeds in notified towns requires a registered Memorandum if creating a formal charge before banks
Right of Redemption (Section 60): "Once a mortgage, always a mortgage"—any "clog on redemption" clause transferring ownership automatically on default is void
Deed Release After Payment: Execute & register a Deed of Redemption (Re-conveyance) at the Sub-Registry and revoke any IGPA

sections.h2: Types of Property Mortgages Recognized Under Section 58 (1882 Act)
sections.content:
Under Section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882, property security falls into distinct legal forms with very different enforcement consequences:

  • Simple Mortgage (Section 58(b)): The borrower binds themselves personally to repay and agrees the lender may apply to court for decree and judicial sale of the mortgaged land upon default—possession stays with the owner.
  • Mortgage by Conditional Sale (Section 58(c)): Property is ostensibly sold subject to a condition that the sale becomes void upon repayment (frequently abused in private village lending—note the Amendment requiring the condition to be inside the same document).
  • Usufructuary Mortgage (Section 58(d) / Khaikhalashi): Possession is handed to the lender to recover principal/interest from rent or agricultural yield.
  • Mortgage by Deposit of Title Deeds (Section 58(f) / Equitable Mortgage): Delivery of original title deeds in specified cities (including Dhaka, Chattogram, Khulna) with intent to create security.

sections.h2: Equitable Mortgage vs. Registered Mortgage + Irrevocable Power of Attorney
sections.content:
Commercial banks in Bangladesh rarely rely solely on an unregistered deposit of deeds. Under Section 59 of the 1882 Act and Section 17 of the Registration Act 1908, loans over BDT 100 typically involve two simultaneously registered instruments at the Sub-Registry:

  1. Registered Mortgage Deed: Creating a recorded encumbrance searchable by subsequent buyers in Sub-Registry Index-II; and
  2. Irrevocable General Power of Attorney (IGPA): Granting the bank statutory authority under Section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 to sell the mortgaged property out of court after default notice without awaiting a full suit decree.

sections.h2: Section 60 Right of Redemption & Unlawful "Clogs on Redemption"
sections.content:
One of the strongest protections for property owners under Section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882 is the equitable maxim: "Once a mortgage, always a mortgage."

Any private loan agreement or supplemental undertaking stating that if the borrower misses an installment date, the property automatically transfers to the lender permanently—known legally as a Clog on Redemption—is null and void. Until a competent court passes a final foreclosure decree or concludes a lawful auction under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003, the borrower retains an absolute right to tender principal plus lawful interest and redeem the land.

sections.h2: How to Reclaim Original Title Deeds & Register a Redemption Deed After Repayment
sections.content:
Many borrowers pay off their home loan or business facility yet neglect formal release—discovering years later that they cannot sell or mutate the land cleanly. Follow these mandatory steps:

  • Obtain No Objection Certificate (NOC) & Clearance: Collect a formal bank Loan Closure Certificate confirming zero outstanding liability across all linked facilities.
  • Collect Full Chain of Title Deeds: Retrieve your original Saf Kabala deed, Bia deeds, CS/SA/RS/BS khatian copies, and mutation DCR held in bank custody.
  • Register Redemption Deed (Re-conveyance) & Cancel IGPA: Where the mortgage and IGPA were registered at the Sub-Registry, execute and register a Deed of Redemption / Release (plus formal revocation of the IGPA) so the encumbrance is erased from public land records.
  • If a Bank Unfairly Withholds Deeds: Under Section 60, lenders cannot retain title deeds for unrelated unmortgaged third-party loans without express cross-collateral agreement. Serve an advocate legal notice and file a Redemption Suit in Civil Court (or Bangladesh Bank / writ complaint if statutory abuse occurs).

sections.h2: Challenging Illegal Bank Auction Notices Under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003
sections.content: If a bank publishes a Section 12 auction tender notice despite full/substantial repayment, disputed interest calculations, or failure to serve mandatory 15-day redemption notices, owners can seek immediate legal protection—including objections before the Artha Rin Adalat, civil declarations challenging forged/unconsented mortgages, or High Court Writ Petitions where banks breach mandatory statutory steps.

faqs.q: Can a bank keep my land deed after I fully repay my home loan because another business loan is pending?
faqs.a: Only if your original Mortgage Deed or facility sanction letter explicitly included a valid cross-collateralization clause covering that specific loan. Otherwise, withholding your original deeds after full payment violates your Section 60 Right of Redemption.

faqs.q: Is a private loan against an original land deed valid without Sub-Registry registration?
faqs.a: Handing over deeds privately outside notified towns or without proper documentation often sparks fraud disputes; moreover, under Section 59, mortgages (other than valid Section 58(f) equitable deposits in notified towns) require registered instruments attested by two witnesses.

faqs.q: What happens if the bank lost my original Sale Deed while in mortgage custody?
faqs.a: The bank must immediately lodge a police GD, bear expenses to obtain certified duplicate copies from the Sub-Registry, issue a formal Loss Indemnity & Non-Encumbrance Certificate, and remain liable for civil compensation if marketability is impaired.
